page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is configured with 32 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic extensions. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-highcpu-16 demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core score of 2926.98, which ranks in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 23457.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10397.0. Memory performance is highly competitive, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and uncached read bandwidth reaching 80.47 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves a strong text generation speed of 301.82 tokens per second during small-scale LLM inference, while maintaining average throughput in static web serving and Redis SET operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-16 offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio tailored for CPU-bound applications that do not require massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution times without the performance degradation associated with shared-core environments. This profile makes the instance highly suitable for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, image processing, ray tracing, and web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. With 8 physical cores and a 2.0 GB per vCPU memory ratio, it is designed for CPU-intensive workloads. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU execution and memory subsystem efficiency, placing both stress-ng single-core and PassMark memory scores in the top 25%. Multi-core compute, web serving throughput, and database operations perform in the average tier. This hardware profile delivers predictable performance for compute-bound tasks without the overhead of excess memory. It is well-suited for software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and moderate-scale web serving.
